extracted.intended_audience: inventors, design patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys preparing U.S. design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing U.S. design patent applications with emphasis on drawing content, scope of protection, statutory requirements, and specification drafting per 37 C.F.R. 1.154. Focused on how to depict claimed design elements and related filing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent statutory basis (35 U.S.C. § 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs: Whoever invents any new, original and ornamental design for an article of manufacture may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish that the claimed subject matter is a 'new, original and ornamental design' for an article of manufacture. This statutory language frames all patentability and drafting considerations for design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs must be: new, original, ornamental, and for an article of manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or drafting, ensure the design is novel and original compared to prior art, is ornamental (i.e., aesthetic rather than purely functional), and is tied to an article of manufacture (not a disembodied design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design must be for an article of manufacture (no disembodied designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design 'for an article' — design must be associated with an article of manufacture; disembodied designs are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings and claims tie the design to a physical article. Avoid claiming a purely abstract or disembodied surface without showing it embodied in an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of protection — types of design subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of protection can cover: surface ornamentation applied to an article; configuration embodied in an article; or configuration and surface ornamentation for an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the claimed design covers surface ornamentation, the overall configuration, or both, and depict drawings accordingly to capture the intended scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design may be directed to less than an entire article
rubrics_metrics.description: A design may be directed to less than an entire article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may claim a portion or feature of an article (e.g., a handle, a surface pattern). When doing so, depict the portion clearly, and use broken lines for unclaimed parts (see broken-line guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single claim requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one claim is permitted in a design patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft a single claim that adequately defines the design as shown in the drawings; use drawings and specification to delineate what is claimed rather than multiple claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection limited to visual appearance 'described' in the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Protects the overall visual appearance of the design 'described' in the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings function as the description of the claimed design; ensure they fully and accurately depict the visual features to be protected because protection is limited to that depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/term/procedural notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent term: 15 year term from date of issue; 6 month period for foreign priority benefit; no provisional design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan filing and priority strategies accordingly (no provisional filings for designs). Note term length for enforcement/licensing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — show all parts of the design you claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings: Show all parts of the design you claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every feature you want protected is depicted in the drawings. Missing elements in drawings may limit the scope of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — perspective views are helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspective is helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspective views where appropriate to convey three-dimensional aspects and overall appearance; supplement with other views as needed for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — show unclaimed parts in broken lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Show parts not claimed with broken lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines to indicate environment or unclaimed portions of the article so the claimed design portion is distinguished from the remainder of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting separated parts and assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: Separated parts may be displayed as part of the whole design (examples: assembled teapot, exploded teapot, teapot with insert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may show components separately to illustrate how parts relate to the claimed design, but be mindful that portions shown separately along with the whole do not receive separate protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including alternative configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative configurations can be included in the same design drawing set (example: coffee machine with alternative position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict alternative positions or configurations within the same application when they represent the same overall design concept; clarity in drawings is required to show alternatives are part of the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portions shown separately do not get separate protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions shown separately along with the whole do not get separate protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing a portion separately for clarity does not by itself create an independent claim to that portion; consider separate applications if separate protection is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants inclusion standard (obvious differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants of a design may be included in the same patent when the differences are 'obvious' in view of case law or the prior art of record (citing In re Stevens, 81 USPQ 362 (CCPA 1949)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include minor variants whose differences involve only ordinary skill (e.g., exact proportioning) within the same application; for non-obvious variants consider separate patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy — multiple design patents for separate portions or variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate patents can be used to receive protection for separate portions; separate patents covering variants of a design provide thorough protection; each design is considered 'patentably distinct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where thorough protection is desired, file multiple design patent applications covering separate portions or distinct variants to obtain distinct patents rather than relying on a single application to cover all variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content and formal arrangement (37 C.F.R. 1.154)
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application has essentially the elements required of an application for a utility patent. The arrangement of the elements of a design patent application and the sections of the specification are as specified in 37 CFR 1.154.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 C.F.R. 1.154 in organizing the application. Include required parts such as drawings and a specification that describes each figure, broken lines, and the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — describe each figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification: Describe each figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written description of every drawing figure to clarify what is depicted and to support claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — describe broken lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification: Describe broken lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state in the specification which portions are shown in broken lines and that such broken lines indicate unclaimed elements or environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification — include the claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification: Include claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the single required design claim in the specification, tied to and supported by the drawings and figure descriptions.
